findings.issue_text: Host comparison in website_name logic is case-sensitive: URI(...).host preserves user-typed case while Discourse.current_hostname is lowercase, so URLs like http://Example.com/user on an example.com instance fall through all branches and display just 'Example.com' instead of the full path; fix is to compare website_host.downcase against discourse_host (also affects the suffix check)

rescue nil at app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:136 swallows URI parse errors: malformed websites cause website_name to become nil while include_website_name still returns true, so the serializer emits website_name: null and the template hides the website row entirely despite a clickable model.website existing, masking the parse failure instead of degrading to showing the raw host

Malformed or scheme-less URLs silently yield no website display because URI() with rescue nil returns nil and the template renders nothing, swallowing the error with no fallback

Missing edge-case test for same-domain website URL with no path, which produces trailing slash in website_name (e.g. 'example.com/')

Sibling-subdomain heuristic incorrectly treats same-label-count hosts on shared/public-suffix domains (e.g. *.herokuapp.com, *.blogspot.com) as same-site, showing full paths for unrelated sites — a display-level phishing vector

goldens.comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Host comparison in website_name logic is case-sensitive: URI(...).host preserves user-typed case while Discourse.current_hostname is lowercase, so URLs like http://Example.com/user on an example.com instance fall through all branches and display just 'Example.com' instead of the full path; fix is to compare website_host.downcase against discourse_host (also affects the suffix check)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `website_host = URI(website.to_s).host` being compared to `Discourse.current_hostname`, but it does not establish that `URI(...).host` preserves user-provided case. Without that fact, the claim that case differences cause the logic to fall through (and thus display only the host) is not verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: rescue nil at app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:136 swallows URI parse errors: malformed websites cause website_name to become nil while include_website_name still returns true, so the serializer emits website_name: null and the template hides the website row entirely despite a clickable model.website existing, masking the parse failure instead of degrading to showing the raw host

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, `website_host = URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` will return `nil` for malformed/unparseable `website` values while `include_website_name` only checks `website.present?`, so the serializer can emit `website_name: null` even when `website` is set. The template was changed to gate the entire website display on `{{#if model.website_name}}`, so a present-but-malformed `model.website` would no longer be shown/linked at all, masking the error and breaking display compared to the previous client-side `websiteName` behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Query strings and fragments are silently dropped from the displayed path because only URI#path is appended, making the displayed link text not match the actual href

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, the displayed text is built as `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path` in several branches, which necessarily omits any `?query` and `#fragment` components. Meanwhile the rendered link `href` remains `model.website` (full URL). So for URLs containing query strings/fragments, the visible text can differ from the actual destination. The diff doesn’t state whether this omission is intended, and no tests cover query/fragment cases, making this a concrete edge-case concern rather than a clearly provable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Malformed or scheme-less URLs silently yield no website display because URI() with rescue nil returns nil and the template renders nothing, swallowing the error with no fallback

adjudication.rationale: In `user_serializer.rb`, `website_name` does `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` and returns early if `website_host` is nil. The template only renders the website block when `model.website_name` is truthy (`{{#if model.website_name}}`), so scheme-less/malformed `website` values can result in no website display with no fallback even though `website` itself is present (`include_website_name` is based only on `website.present?`). This is a diff-grounded robustness/edge-case concern rather than a clearly verifiable defect, since the diff doesn’t establish whether scheme-less URLs are allowed/expected input.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Subdomain heuristic conflates label-count equality with domain-family matching on multi-label TLDs, producing inconsistent results across ad-hoc branches

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, the branch `elsif (website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length) && discourse_host.split('.').length > 2` treats equal label-count hosts as potentially the same “domain family” by comparing `split('.')[1..-1]` (e.g., `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`). This heuristic breaks on multi-label public suffixes like `co.uk`: `foo.co.uk` and `bar.co.uk` have equal label counts (>2) and share `split[1..] == 'co.uk'`, so the code would incorrectly treat them as related and append the path (`website_host + URI(...).path`). That yields inconsistent/incorrect `website_name` values depending on TLD structure, as the finding describes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: URI(website.to_s) is parsed redundantly per attribute call (up to twice per serialization) adding avoidable cost in a hot path

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, `URI(website.to_s)` is instantiated multiple times: once to compute `website_host = URI(website.to_s).host` and again in branches that append `URI(website.to_s).path` (`website_host + URI(website.to_s).path`). This redundant parsing is visible in the diff and could be avoided by parsing once and reusing the result (especially relevant if serializer methods are called frequently).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing test case for the elsif branch's false path in website_name serializer (sibling subdomain of instance domain, e.g. forums.example.com vs other.example.com)

adjudication.rationale: The new `website_name` serializer adds a nontrivial `elsif` branch for cases where `website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length` and the length is `> 2`, with a ternary that can return either `website_host + path` or just `website_host`. In the added specs, `user.user_profile.website` is always `http://example.com/user` (host has only 2 labels), so this `elsif` branch is never exercised at all—meaning there is indeed missing test coverage for the `elsif` logic, including its false/else outcome.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing edge-case test for same-domain website URL with no path, which produces trailing slash in website_name (e.g. 'example.com/')

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial `website_name` logic in `UserSerializer#website_name` that returns `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path` when the website domain matches `Discourse.current_hostname`. The new specs only cover the same-domain case with a non-empty path (`http://example.com/user`) and do not cover the edge case where the URL has no path (e.g. `http://example.com` or `http://example.com/`), which could affect whether the returned `website_name` includes a trailing "/" depending on `URI(...).path`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing test for invalid/malformed website URLs (e.g. 'not a url' or scheme-less 'example.com'), leaving fallback behavior unverified

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial parsing logic in `UserSerializer#website_name` using `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` and conditionally returns `nil` when parsing fails, while `include_website_name` includes the field whenever `website.present?`. The added specs only cover a well-formed `http://example.com/user` URL and do not exercise malformed or scheme-less inputs (e.g., `not a url`, `example.com/user`) where `URI(...).host` would be `nil` and the JSON may include `website_name: null`. This edge-case behavior is new/important and currently untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No frontend test for removed websiteName computed property in user.js.es6; code relying on it (themes/plugins) silently breaks

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the `websiteName` computed property from `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/user.js.es6` and updates the template to use `model.website_name` instead. While core template usage is updated, this is an implicit API change: any themes/plugins that referenced `controller.websiteName` would no longer work, and there is no frontend/acceptance test in the diff that would catch such a regression. This is a real compatibility/test-coverage concern grounded in the removed property, but not a verifiable core defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing test that website_name is absent from JSON when website is blank, so include_website_name guard could be broken without a failing test

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new serialized field `:website_name` with an `include_website_name` guard (`def include_website_name; website.present?; end`) in `user_serializer.rb`, and adds specs only for cases where `user.user_profile.website` is set. The shown spec additions do not cover the blank/absent website case to ensure `website_name` is omitted from the JSON, so a regression in `include_website_name` could slip through without a failing test.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Tests stub Discourse.current_hostname instead of exercising real hostname resolution/SiteSetting configuration, risking interface drift going undetected

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb`, the new `website_name` behavior is tested by stubbing `Discourse.current_hostname` (e.g., `Discourse.stubs(:current_hostname).returns('forums.example.com')`) rather than exercising whatever real hostname resolution/configuration path `Discourse.current_hostname` uses. This is a specific, diff-grounded test strategy concern: if the implementation of `Discourse.current_hostname` changes (or its coupling to settings changes), these tests may still pass without catching the drift, even though `website_name` depends on that value.

adjudication_records.issue_text: website_name may be missing in serializer contexts that don't include it (other serializers, cached payloads, user card), silently dropping the website display since the client no longer computes websiteName as a fallback

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, the client-side computed `websiteName` is removed and the template is updated to use `model.website_name`. The same diff also updates `UserSerializer` to expose `:website_name` (with `include_website_name` gated on `website.present?`), plus adds specs covering it. The finding’s concern about “other serializers, cached payloads, user card” is not shown or verifiable from the provided diff, so we can’t confirm a real break from this PR alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Sibling-subdomain heuristic incorrectly treats same-label-count hosts on shared/public-suffix domains (e.g. *.herokuapp.com, *.blogspot.com) as same-site, showing full paths for unrelated sites — a display-level phishing vector

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, the `elsif` branch treats hosts with the same number of dot-labels as “sibling subdomains” and, if their suffix matches (`website_host.split('.')[1..-1] == discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1]`), returns `website_host + URI(...).path`. This will incorrectly consider shared/public-suffix style domains (e.g. `a.herokuapp.com` vs `b.herokuapp.com`, both 3 labels, `> 2`) as same-site and include the full path for an unrelated site. That behavior is directly introduced by the heuristic in this diff and could mislead users (display-level phishing risk).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Sibling branch only fires when label counts are equal, so instance forums.example.com with website www.forums.example.com is not treated as same-site and never shows the path

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, the “sibling subdomain” branch only runs when `website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length` (and > 2). For `discourse_host = forums.example.com` (3 labels) and `website_host = www.forums.example.com` (4 labels), that branch is skipped and the final `ends_with?('.' << website_host)` check also won’t match, so it will return just `website_host` (no path). The finding correctly points out an unhandled edge case in the new same-site/path logic, but whether `www.forums.example.com` should be treated as “same-site” is a product/behavior expectation not proven by the diff/tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Website path is appended without stripping query strings/fragments, so URLs like http://example.com/t?secret=x display with the query string included

adjudication.rationale: In `user_serializer.rb#website_name`, when appending the path it uses `URI(website.to_s).path`, which excludes query strings and fragments by definition (it does not use `.query` or `.fragment`). Therefore a URL like `http://example.com/t?secret=x` would yield `example.com/t`, not include `?secret=x`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Confusingly similar host like forums.example.com.evil.com is displayed as-is when label counts match, though this is not a regression from prior behavior

adjudication.rationale: The new `website_name` logic in `user_serializer.rb` always returns `website_host` (or `website_host + path` when the host matches the instance or a recognized parent-domain relationship). For the example `forums.example.com.evil.com` with an instance like `forums.example.com`, the label-count branch does not apply (counts differ), and the code falls through to returning `website_host` unchanged. Nothing in the diff indicates a special “label counts match” case that would newly cause this specific host to be treated incorrectly; it is simply displayed as its host, consistent with prior behavior of showing the host portion.
